claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component itself; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Pulumi's component state migrations are a new feature (recently introduced).
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A GitHub discussion for component state migrations feedback exists at github.com/pulumi/pulumi/discussions/24799.
A Pulumi docs page exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ covering the component state migrations callback contract.
The pulumi/examples repository contains the aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration example with v1, v2, and v3 programs and migration code.
Pulumi components are documented at /docs/iac/concepts/components/ and let users turn a group of resources into a reusable building block.
The legacy AWSX component `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` in the example's v1 creates a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and its association, and an internet gateway.
Replacing an AWS VPC forces replacement of a security group that refers to the VPC's ID (per the AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId documentation).
If a database is recreated, its replacement does not automatically contain the old data.
The modern AWSX component is `awsx.ec2.Vpc`.
The v3 version of the example removes AWSX and declares resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
In the example, across all three versions the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.

In the example, the Pulumi resource tree for v1 (legacy awsx:x:ec2:Vpc with awsx:x:ec2:Subnet and awsx:x:ec2:InternetGateway wrappers), v2 (awsx:ec2:Vpc containing aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc with subnet 'vpc-isolated-1', route table, association, internet gateway), and v3 (aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc at the root) is as shown.
Pulumi state records both physical resources and components; each record has a Pulumi name called a URN, and managed resources also have a provider ID such as an AWS VPC ID.
Legacy AWSX wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components, while modern AWSX removes those wrappers and places managed resources under different parents.
In the example, the Pulumi name of the subnet changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1` between legacy and modern AWSX.

Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when its saved state remains compatible, but cannot remove component wrappers or transfer references to replacement resources; a state migration does that.
Pulumi component resources accept a `stateMigrations` option that registers a migration callback, used together with an alias for the legacy component type.
A state migration callback receives the saved state of the aliased old component followed by the state of its children.

A state migration callback returns `newState` (the complete set of records replacing the old component and its children) and `successors` (a map from each disappearing old URN to the URN that takes its place).
In the example migration, the callback is idempotent: if state already uses modern AWSX or plain AWS resources it does nothing, and an unexpected component type raises an error.
In the example, the `rename` helper copies the saved record and changes its URN, type, and parent, preserving the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.

Pulumi uses the `successors` mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, keeping the security group's reference connected to the migrated VPC record with the same AWS VPC ID.
The example's second migration removes the AWSX VPC component record and maps both the old component and its VPC child to the new VPC record, keeping the VPC's AWS ID.

Pulumi runs state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a stack on legacy AWSX can upgrade directly to plain AWS, a stack on modern AWSX skips the first migration, and once both have run, callbacks return no result on later updates.

After a migration changes saved state, Pulumi compares the new program with that state and calls the provider for remaining changes; the example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
`pulumi preview` evaluates a state migration without saving it, and `pulumi up` saves the migrated state.
When upgrading the example between versions, the preview should show no creates, deletes, or replacements for the existing VPC, subnet, route table, association, internet gateway, and security group.

When users upgrade a component that registers a migration internally, Pulumi runs the migration automatically as part of normal preview and update, without users writing the migration, attaching the callback, or editing stack state.
For internal component changes that keep the same inputs and outputs, users can keep their existing component calls.
Pulumi state migration callbacks (the state migrations resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must be idempotent and must return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
Pulumi state migration callbacks rewrite resource state without performing provider operations.

A Pulumi component state migration (the `stateMigrations` resource option callback) is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN that is omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a component state migration callback returns no result.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/ has a #callback-api section explaining the callback API.

Component state migration callback state entries use the checkpoint resource format documented in the Pulumi developer docs deployment schema (pulumi-resource-state), including fields such as `urn`, `type`, `id`, `parent`, `provider`, `inputs`, and `outputs`.

The Pulumi developer docs page at pulumi-developer-docs.readthedocs.io/latest/docs/references/deployment-schema.html has a #pulumi-resource-state section describing the checkpoint resource state format.

For component state migrations, resources pending deletion in the subtree block a state-changing migration; the unfinished deletion must be completed with the migration returning no changes before retrying.
For component state migrations, persisted snippet references that would need to change block a state-changing migration and must be updated or removed first.
A component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using Pulumi update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing results of component state migrations (under update plans or targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied migration.
